questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: Why can small dissolved substances move directly from the cytoplasm of one living plant cell to that of its neighbour?

options.text: The cells are linked by plasmodesmata.
options.why: Cytoplasmic channels cross the cell walls.

options.text: The cells share a nucleus.
options.why: Each cell retains its own nucleus.
options.whyWrong: Each cell retains its own nucleus.

options.text: The cell walls are made of phospholipids.
options.why: Phospholipids form membranes. Cellulose forms much of the primary plant cell wall.
options.whyWrong: Phospholipids form membranes. Cellulose forms much of the primary plant cell wall.

options.text: The two cells are joined by a xylem vessel.
options.why: Xylem carries water over distances. The question asks about direct contact between adjacent cytoplasms.
options.whyWrong: Xylem carries water over distances. The question asks about direct contact between adjacent cytoplasms.

questions.hint: Look for channels crossing a cell wall.
questions.explanation: Cytoplasmic channels cross the cell walls.
questions.trap: Each cell retains its own nucleus.
questions.mnemonic: Look for channels crossing a cell wall.

askPresets.answer: Cytoplasmic channels cross the cell walls.
Each cell retains its own nucleus.

options.whyWrong: Cellulose is a structural polysaccharide in plant cell walls.

options.text: Glycogen
options.why: Glycogen stores carbohydrate in many organisms.
options.whyWrong: Glycogen stores carbohydrate in many organisms.

options.text: DNA
options.why: DNA stores hereditary information.
options.whyWrong: DNA stores hereditary information.

questions.hint: Think of molecules with water-attracting heads and water-repelling tails.
questions.explanation: Phospholipids form the bilayer.
questions.trap: Cellulose is a structural polysaccharide in plant cell walls.
questions.mnemonic: Think of molecules with water-attracting heads and water-repelling tails.

askPresets.answer: Phospholipids form the bilayer.
Cellulose is a structural polysaccharide in plant cell walls.

options.whyWrong: Chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis. They are not the main starch-storage plastids in cassava roots.

options.text: Chromoplasts
options.why: Chromoplasts accumulate pigments.
options.whyWrong: Chromoplasts accumulate pigments.

options.text: Amyloplasts
options.why: Amyloplasts specialise in starch storage.

options.text: Ribosomes
options.why: Ribosomes make proteins and are not plastids.
options.whyWrong: Ribosomes make proteins and are not plastids.

questions.hint: The prefix refers to starch.
questions.explanation: Amyloplasts specialise in starch storage.
questions.trap: Chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis. They are not the main starch-storage plastids in cassava roots.

questions.stem: What is the name of the membrane surrounding a plant cell’s central vacuole?

options.text: Nuclear envelope

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: How does a cell take in a large particle by endocytosis?

options.text: The particle passes through a channel protein.
options.why: Channel proteins pass selected ions or small molecules.
options.whyWrong: Channel proteins pass selected ions or small molecules.

options.text: The particle dissolves directly in the lipid bilayer.
options.why: Large particles cannot dissolve into the bilayer as small non-polar molecules can.
options.whyWrong: Large particles cannot dissolve into the bilayer as small non-polar molecules can.

options.text: The surface membrane encloses it in a vesicle.
options.why: The cell membrane surrounds the particle and buds inward.

options.text: The particle enters through a nuclear pore.
options.why: Nuclear pores regulate exchange with the nucleus.
options.whyWrong: Nuclear pores regulate exchange with the nucleus.

questions.hint: Follow what the plasma membrane does around the particle.
questions.explanation: The cell membrane surrounds the particle and buds inward.
questions.trap: Channel proteins pass selected ions or small molecules.
questions.mnemonic: Follow what the plasma membrane does around the particle.

askPresets.answer: The cell membrane surrounds the particle and buds inward.

questions.stem: Which feature of mitochondria supports the idea that their ancestors were free-living cells?

options.text: Mitochondria contain their own DNA.
options.why: Their own DNA is among the lines of evidence for endosymbiosis.

options.text: Mitochondria contain cellulose walls.
options.why: Mitochondria have membranes rather than cellulose walls.
options.whyWrong: Mitochondria have membranes rather than cellulose walls.

options.text: Mitochondria are found only in plants.
options.why: Mitochondria occur in animal cells and many other eukaryotes as well.
options.whyWrong: Mitochondria occur in animal cells and many other eukaryotes as well.

options.text: Mitochondria store all of the cell’s chromosomes.
options.why: Most chromosomes of a eukaryotic cell are in its nucleus.
options.whyWrong: Most chromosomes of a eukaryotic cell are in its nucleus.

questions.hint: Look for a feature that reflects a formerly separate genome.
questions.explanation: Their own DNA is among the lines of evidence for endosymbiosis.
questions.trap: Mitochondria have membranes rather than cellulose walls.
questions.mnemonic: Look for a feature that reflects a formerly separate genome.

askPresets.answer: Their own DNA is among the lines of evidence for endosymbiosis.
Mitochondria have membranes rather than cellulose walls.

questions.stem: A flood leaves a small, chance sample of a large lizard population alive. Which process can explain a resulting change in allele frequencies even if the alleles did not affect survival?

options.text: Natural selection

options.whyWrong: Natural selection requires survival or reproduction to differ in a way associated with a heritable trait.

options.text: Gene flow
options.why: Gene flow transfers alleles between populations through migration and reproduction.
options.whyWrong: Gene flow transfers alleles between populations through migration and reproduction.

options.text: Artificial selection
options.why: Artificial selection involves human choice of which organisms reproduce.
options.whyWrong: Artificial selection involves human choice of which organisms reproduce.

questions.hint: Focus on what survives by chance.
questions.explanation: A population bottleneck can change allele frequencies by chance.
questions.trap: Natural selection requires survival or reproduction to differ in a way associated with a heritable trait.
questions.mnemonic: Focus on what survives by chance.

askPresets.answer: A population bottleneck can change allele frequencies by chance.
Natural selection requires survival or reproduction to differ in a way associated with a heritable trait.

options.whyWrong: Starch digestion yields sugars rather than amino acids.

options.text: It increases the surface exposed to enzymes.
options.why: Smaller pieces expose more surface to the digestive juices.

options.text: It raises the yam to the enzymes’ optimum temperature.
options.why: Breaking food apart does not help mainly by changing its temperature.
options.whyWrong: Breaking food apart does not help mainly by changing its temperature.

options.text: It removes all the fibre from the yam.
options.why: Fibre is not removed by chewing.
options.whyWrong: Fibre is not removed by chewing.

questions.stem: Why can a person become deficient in vitamin C despite getting enough energy from food?

options.text: The body manufactures vitamin C only during fasting.
options.why: Humans do not manufacture vitamin C in appreciable quantities.
options.whyWrong: Humans do not manufacture vitamin C in appreciable quantities.

options.text: Vitamin C is used up in direct proportion to the amount of water drunk.
options.why: Water intake is not the process described in this question.
options.whyWrong: Water intake is not the process described in this question.

options.text: Vitamin C supplies no energy, so it must come from foods such as fresh fruit and vegetables.
options.why: Food energy and vitamin C are separate needs. Humans cannot make enough vitamin C, so a diet of energy-rich staples with little fresh fruit or vegetables can still lack it.

options.text: Sufficient dietary energy prevents the absorption of vitamin C.
options.why: Getting enough energy does not prevent the intestine from absorbing vitamin C.
options.whyWrong: Getting enough energy does not prevent the intestine from absorbing vitamin C.

questions.hint: Calories and vitamins are different things.
questions.explanation: Food energy and vitamin C are separate needs. Humans cannot make enough vitamin C, so a diet of energy-rich staples with little fresh fruit or vegetables can still lack it.

questions.mnemonic: Calories and vitamins are different things.

askPresets.answer: Food energy and vitamin C are separate needs. Humans cannot make enough vitamin C, so a diet of energy-rich staples with little fresh fruit or vegetables can still lack it.
Humans do not manufacture vitamin C in appreciable quantities.

questions.stem: Why does removing a complete ring of bark and phloem from a woody stem cause sugars to accumulate just above the cut?

options.why: Xylem mainly transports water and dissolved mineral ions.
options.whyWrong: Xylem mainly transports water and dissolved mineral ions.

options.why: The cut in the stem does not directly prevent gas entry into the leaves.

options.whyWrong: Pulmonary veins bring blood from the lungs to the left atrium.

options.text: To return blood from the legs to the right atrium

questions.stem: Which organelle’s genes are ordinarily passed to a human child through the egg’s cytoplasm?

options.text: The mitochondrion
options.why: Human mitochondrial DNA is ordinarily inherited from the mother.

options.text: The Golgi apparatus
options.why: The Golgi apparatus has no separate genome.
options.whyWrong: The Golgi apparatus has no separate genome.

options.text: The lysosome
options.why: Lysosomes contain digestive enzymes but no separate genome.
options.whyWrong: Lysosomes contain digestive enzymes but no separate genome.

options.text: The centriole

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: Why can a female cat heterozygous for two X-linked coat-colour alleles have patches of different colours?

options.text: Every hair follicle changes its DNA each time a hair grows.
options.why: The alleles need not change for different patches to express different colours.
options.whyWrong: The alleles need not change for different patches to express different colours.

options.text: Different X chromosomes are inactive in different groups of skin cells.
options.why: Descendants of each cell generally retain the same inactive X chromosome.

options.text: Each skin cell produces an extra copy of the Y chromosome.
options.why: A typical female cat with two X chromosomes does not produce copies of a Y chromosome in skin cells.
options.whyWrong: A typical female cat with two X chromosomes does not produce copies of a Y chromosome in skin cells.

options.text: Both alleles are always switched off in all skin cells.
options.why: Inactivation normally leaves one X active in each cell.
options.whyWrong: Inactivation normally leaves one X active in each cell.

questions.hint: Consider which X remains active in each patch.
questions.explanation: Descendants of each cell generally retain the same inactive X chromosome.
questions.trap: The alleles need not change for different patches to express different colours.
questions.mnemonic: Consider which X remains active in each patch.

askPresets.answer: Descendants of each cell generally retain the same inactive X chromosome.
The alleles need not change for different patches to express different colours.
